answer: In this PoA design, identity verification binds each agent to a Wesolowski VDF: a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings in which every state depends on the previous one. GPUs can verify proofs concurrently, but cannot split one chain across processors for proportional speedup. Thus, simulating many cloned identities imposes a strict physical wall-clock cost; ripple, lotus, and ocean are merely labels, not substitutes for elapsed computation.
